title: Active-drainage MODFLOW6 tangent closure

canonical.relevant_delta_since_f_gc30: NO_SRC_RUNTIME_SOLVER_TRANSACTION_DELTA; only publication P2E08 files in the observed 10-commit advancement

objective: Close only the active-drainage derivative coverage needed by the already-admitted MODFLOW6 SWAP predictor-response contract, without reopening F-GC30 or changing the frozen Drainage-v1 denominator.

reconcile_findings.production_drainage_tangent: Per-level drainage response already exposes derivative_defined and dq_dgroundwater_level; the missing process chain is qbot -> accepted hydraulic state -> derived groundwater_level -> next-step drainage response -> later hydraulic state.
reconcile_findings.serialized_runtime_order: Active drainage is evaluated from request/base-state groundwater_level before a Richards trial and is held fixed during that solve.
reconcile_findings.current_groundwater_level_lifecycle: The serialized reference state binding seeds solver gwl from the incoming physical state; inspected HeadCalc code does not generally recompute gwl on the prescribed-qbot route; the solve result copies state_binding%gwl into candidate_state%groundwater_level; the runtime then copies that candidate value into physical%groundwater_level.
reconcile_findings.legacy_order: Legacy SWAP ordering is Drainage -> SoilWater(2) -> accepted/retry resolution -> SoilWater(3); SoilWater(3) calls calcgwl, so the newly derived groundwater level becomes input to the next physical step rather than an implicit within-solve drainage update.
reconcile_findings.production_lifecycle_gap: For the inspected serialized prescribed-qbot route, the legacy post-solve derived-state calcgwl update is not presently visible between the accepted hydraulic solution and publication of the next physical state. Therefore a nonzero drainage tangent cannot be added consistently until the physical groundwater-level lifecycle is qualified.
reconcile_findings.drainage_v1_governance: F-PM19/F-TB12 define Drainage-v1 100-percent completion for a frozen eight-variant denominator and explicitly do not require fully implicit drainage-response solver coupling. F-GC32 is a new coupling sensitivity/derived-state capability, not a reopening of Drainage-v1.
reconcile_findings.zero_derivative_disposition: FORBIDDEN_AS_WORKAROUND: setting d(gwl)/d(qbot)=0 would encode the currently frozen technical state value as scientific truth before exact calcgwl-derived-state semantics are qualified.

directional_seam_findings.step_contract: soil_water_accepted_step_direction_request_t carries incoming pressure-head, water-content and ponding directions plus the direct bottom-control derivative; it carries no groundwater-level direction and no source/sink residual direction.
directional_seam_findings.tangent_rhs: F-KT21 reuses the accepted TRIDAG factorization and assembles the directional RHS from incoming storage, conductivity, top-boundary and bottom-control terms. Source/sink derivatives are currently absent because the admitted route assumes those terms are state-independent.
directional_seam_findings.physical_residual_sign: B1.10 vector_F contains +sink-source. Therefore an explicit drainage sink direction contributes with positive sign to dF and with negative sign to the TRIDAG right-hand side J*s = -(B*s_prev + r_p).
directional_seam_findings.trajectory_composer: The transaction trajectory composer correctly promotes only accepted step directions and discards rejected work, but currently propagates no groundwater-level directional scalar.
minimal_future_shape: Use exact calcgwl semantics to derive groundwater_level and dgroundwater_level/dqbot from the accepted/base pressure-head state and its accepted trajectory direction.
Evaluate the already-qualified drainage response at the lagged start-of-step groundwater level.
Multiply each smooth defined dq_dgroundwater_level by the lagged groundwater-level direction and map the resulting drainage sink direction to the existing bottom-lumped node distribution.
Pass that explicit source/sink residual direction into the same accepted-step tangent backsolve; do not place drainage inside the nonlinear Richards Jacobian.

After every accepted physical step, derive and publish the physical groundwater_level with the same exact calcgwl semantics so the tangent is a derivative of the actual production trajectory rather than of a different model.

Implement a separately qualified post-solve derived-groundwater-level service only if exact B0 semantics confirm the recovered lifecycle; preserve physical lagging of drainage per accepted step.

No assumption that modern or third-party calcgwl source equals exact B0.
No tangent implementation that differs from the actual physical production groundwater-level trajectory.
